title: [VSC-26] JetBrains: show delivery check exit codes outside the Int range, matching the daemon and VS Code
description:
Filed by VSC-18 (task-43363b5d). Parked by VSC-3 and VSC-8, and by architect comment-97b50ba7 item 2.
The daemon accepts any safe-integer check exitCode. JetBrains MoeJson.deliveryExitCode returns null outside the Int range (TaskDelivery.exitCode is Int), so a Windows NTSTATUS code such as 3221225477 shows no exit row in JetBrains. VS Code's deliveryRows (Number.isSafeInteger) renders it as FAIL. client-delivery.json deliberately leaves this case unpinned (Serena mem:decision-client-corpus-conventions). Fix in MoeJson.kt and Models.kt (a Long), then add a corpus row so both clients pin the same verdict. JetBrains first.
definitionOfDone: A check run with exitCode 3221225477 renders an exit row with a FAIL verdict in JetBrains DeliveryPresentation, pinned by a new client-delivery.json row that DeliveryCorpusTest.kt replays.
moe-vscode tests/delivery-corpus.test.cjs replays the new row unchanged and passes.
`gradlew.bat test` passes on native Windows under the jetbrains-gradle lease, and moe-vscode `npm test` passes in a git-archive snapshot.

implementationPlan.description:
2. Widen the exit code to Long, the daemon's safe-integer rule. Edit tool only; keep the Kotlin style.

moe-jetbrains/src/main/kotlin/com/moe/model/Models.kt:
- `data class DeliveryCheckRun(... val exitCode: Long? = null ...)`.
- Add one comment line: the daemon accepts any JS safe integer (deliveryProjection.ts, Number.isSafeInteger), e.g. Windows NTSTATUS 3221225477, which overflows Int.
- Leave every other exitCode alone, including TaskVerification's Int (Models.kt about :119): that one is a different contract.

moe-jetbrains/src/main/kotlin/com/moe/util/MoeJson.kt, deliveryExitCode():
- Return Long?.
- Keep the parse exactly as it is: number primitives only, BigDecimal of the literal text, and no coercion of strings or fractions.
- Bound with a private `MAX_SAFE_EXIT = BigDecimal(9007199254740991L)` (2^53-1, Number.MAX_SAFE_INTEGER): `if (value.abs() > MAX_SAFE_EXIT) null else value.longValueExact()`.
- Keep both catch arms: NumberFormatException and ArithmeticException (fractions such as 1.1 and 1e-400) give null.
- Update its KDoc: exact safe integers, the same rule as the daemon and VS Code.

moe-jetbrains/src/main/kotlin/com/moe/toolwindow/DeliveryPresentation.kt:
- Compare with Long literals: `code == 0L`, `code != 0L`. Kotlin refuses Long == Int.
- `code.toString()` is unchanged.
- The verdict rule is unchanged: only exit 0 with no outcome or exactly "passed" passes.

executionContract.intendedBehavior:
JetBrains parses a delivery check exitCode as an exact JS safe integer (|n| <= 2^53-1) into a Long, as the daemon and VS Code do.

An exit code outside the Int range, such as Windows NTSTATUS 3221225477, therefore renders as a failed exit row with its exact decimal value.

Values past the safe range, fractions, strings and non-numbers still parse to null, so they show no exit row.
acceptanceCriteria: client-delivery.json gains D17 (exitCode 3221225477 with command and runner-observed source) and D18 (exitCode 9007199254740991). Both expect a moe.delivery.checkFailed row with the exact decimal and a FAIL verdict, plus their command/source rows.
DeliveryCorpusTest replays D17 and D18 green.
moe-vscode tests/delivery-corpus.test.cjs replays them green with no moe-vscode change.
The full gradlew.bat test on native Windows under the jetbrains-gradle lease and moe-vscode npm test in a git-archive snapshot both pass.
invariants: The pass rule is unchanged: only exit 0 with no outcome or exactly 'passed' passes.
TaskVerification.exitCode stays Int, and no moe-vscode file changes.
The parser never coerces strings, fractions or overflow into a code.
compatibility: Every exit code already in the Int range renders exactly as before; the D01-D16 rows are unchanged.
A legacy or absent exitCode still shows no exit row.
